_README: Recruitment agencies to be REGISTERED with, which is a different thing from
the agencies the pipeline already answers.
THE DIFFERENCE
The main pipeline is reactive: an agency advertises a vacancy, the machine
writes to them about that vacancy. Good, but it only ever reaches the
agencies that happened to advertise something in the last 48 hours.
This file is the other half. A consultant's database is searched by the
consultant, on their own time, against roles that were never advertised -
so being IN the database is inbound, and most desks rank their search
results by how recently a candidate was in touch.
WHY THIS ONE IS ALLOWED TO REPEAT
Everywhere else in this repository the rule is one approach per company,
ever, because a second unsolicited email to an employer reads as
pestering. An agency is the exception the codebase already recognises:
they are PAID to place people, they hold dozens of live roles at once,
and a candidate who checks in every few weeks is a candidate they can
actually place. So the cap here is a long cooldown, not a single shot,
and the second letter is a different letter - a refresh, not the same
pitch sent twice.
'desk' IS THE ONLY THING THE LETTER MAY SAY ABOUT THEM
Same discipline as data/targets.json. One true line about what they
actually recruit for, used as the reason for writing to them rather than
to anyone else. If it is wrong, fix it here; nothing invents its own.
'site' IS SCRAPED, NOT GUESSED
The address is found by the pipeline's ordinary discovery against this
domain and MX-checked before anything is sent. No address in this file,
no pattern-generated ones, and an agency whose site publishes nothing
real is reported and skipped rather than guessed at.
Orion Group is the known case: orionjobs.com carries no MX record, so if
discovery only turns up an @orionjobs.com address there is nothing that
can legitimately be posted to. Their own upload form is the route there.
